description:
We are PloTwist, a team passionate about space exploration, science, and creative storytelling. We want to bring NASA’s forgotten lunar and planetary artifacts back into the spotlight through engaging educational content.

We welcome curious and creative participants interested in research, storytelling, science communication, graphic design, illustration, animation, or web development. All experience levels are welcome!
summary:
Silent Explorers is an interactive educational website that transforms real NASA mission information into an engaging space-discovery experience for children up to approximately 12 years old.

It explores a fascinating question: What happens to spacecraft and equipment after their missions end?

Through colorful visuals, an interactive lunar map, searchable mission records, and an archive covering the Moon, Mars, and deep space, children discover the machines, instruments, and evidence behind space exploration.

The experience follows five simple questions: Where did NASA explore? What equipment was used? What was its purpose? What did scientists learn? What can we investigate next?

Using authentic NASA and NASA/JPL information, PloTwist team encourages curiosity, observation, questioning, evidence-based thinking, and digital literacy.

Rather than overwhelming children with technical databases, it turns scientific information into an accessible journey where every discovery connects a fact, a source, and a new question.
details:
Detailed Project Description – Silent Explorers

Silent Explorers is an interactive, story-driven educational website designed to help children up to approximately 12 years old discover what happens to spacecraft and scientific equipment after their missions end.

What it does

The project transforms real NASA mission information into an accessible space-exploration journey. It covers three exploration areas: the Moon, Mars, and deep space. Instead of presenting children with complex scientific databases, it introduces missions through short explanations, visual clues, interactive maps, searchable records, and questions that encourage further investigation.

How it works

The experience guides children through five stages: Place, Equipment, Purpose, Evidence, and Question.

• Mission Trail: Introduces the stories of silent explorers through five short discovery stages.
• Interactive Moon Map: Displays lunar landing locations, including Apollo mission sites and Surveyor landing sites. Children can select markers to explore locations and related records.
• Lunar Data Explorer: Provides 38 child-friendly records connected to NASA lunar missions. Children can search by keywords and filter records into Hardware, Science, and Mission Records.
• Mission Archive: Allows exploration of Moon, Mars, and deep-space missions, distinguishing between surface artifacts, historical mission records, and spacecraft that continued traveling.
• Live Signal: Connects to NASA's public Near-Earth Object API to introduce children to ongoing space observations. A fallback mechanism helps maintain the experience when API requests are unavailable.
• Calm Mode: Allows children to turn off the optional ambient background audio.

Each discovery connects a scientific fact to its original NASA source and encourages children to ask another question.

Benefits

PloTwist team aims to develop curiosity, observation, critical thinking, evidence-based reasoning, and digital literacy. Children learn to explore information, compare missions, interpret scientific evidence, and distinguish between different types of space missions. Its child-friendly language and interactive design provide an accessible introduction to authentic scientific information without removing the underlying science.

Tools and Technologies

• HTML5: Page structure and content.
• CSS3: Visual design, layouts, and responsive styling.
• JavaScript: Interactive maps, navigation, search, filters, and API integration.
• Node.js: Lightweight static server for local development.
• NASA Open APIs: Live Near-Earth Object data.
• NASA NSSDCA and NASA/JPL: Scientific records and mission information.
• Python, NumPy, and Pillow: Creation of a procedural lunar surface texture.
• Git and GitHub: Source-code management and version control.
• GitHub Pages: Public website hosting.

GitHub Link: https://github.com/ShireenTalaat/PloTwist_NASA

The project uses no third-party runtime dependencies or dedicated hardware. It is accessible through a modern web browser.

Our goal is to simplify the path into real science, turning a NASA archive into an interactive field trip where every record gives a child a fact, a source, and a question.
